intro: Scaling individual coordinates cannot remove cross-feature correlation. A symmetric inverse square root transforms the covariance in all directions.
task: Return the symmetric whitening matrix for a supplied positive-semidefinite covariance, regularized by a positive epsilon.
requirements: covariance is a square symmetric matrix, with symmetry tolerance 1e-10. Its smallest eigenvalue must be at least -1e-10.
epsilon is a scalar in [1e-8,1e6]. Return V diag(1/sqrt(max(eigenvalue,0)+epsilon)) V.T from an orthonormal eigendecomposition.
This is regularized ZCA whitening. Return the transformation matrix, not transformed samples; eigenvector signs must not affect the answer.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: A symmetric covariance has orthogonal eigenvectors and real eigenvalues, which expose its principal directions.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Scale eigenvector columns by inverse square roots of regularized eigenvalues before multiplying by their transpose.

explanation: A covariance eigendecomposition identifies orthogonal directions and their variances. Scaling each direction by the inverse square root and rotating back gives a symmetric transform.

With regularization, W(C+epsilon I)W.T equals identity up to numerical error. W C W.T instead retains a small regularization-dependent shrinkage, so it should not be claimed to equal identity exactly.
